passages.scripture: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?

lines.text: Paul speaks to his brothers.
Paul speaks to those who know the law of Moses.
The law rules over a person while he lives.
After a person dies, the law does not rule over them.

passages.scripture: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.

lines.text: A married woman is bound by the law of marriage to her husband.
This law only applies as long as her husband lives.
If her husband dies, the law no longer binds a wife to her husband.
If a wife becomes a widow, then she is released from the law of marriage.

passages.scripture: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress, even if she marries another man.

lines.text: A married woman is bound by law to her husband while he lives.
If a married woman has sexual relations another man while her husband is alive, people call her an adulteress.
However, if her husband dies, she is free from the law of her marriage.
If woman marries another man after her husband dies, she is not an adulteress.

passages.scripture: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.

lines.text: Paul speaks to his brothers in Christ.
Paul says his brothers died to the law.
We died to the law.
We died to the law through the body of Christ.
We died to the law so that we would belong to Christ.
Christ was raised from the dead.
God raised Christ from the dead.
We belong to Christ so that we will bear fruit for God.

passages.scripture: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.

lines.text: We once lived according to the flesh.
We followed our sinful nature.
Sinful passions controlled us.
The law aroused these sinful passions.
These sinful passions worked in our bodies.
These sinful passions produced results that led to death.

passages.scripture: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.

lines.text: We were bound by our sinful passions.
But then we died to what once held us captive.
We are now released from the law.
We serve in a new way.
This new way we serve is the way of the Spirit.
We do not serve in the old way.
The old way we served was the way of the written code.

passages.scripture: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”

lines.text: The law reveals the difference between good and evil.
The only way Paul knew about sin, was because the law revealed the difference right and wrong.
For example, the law says, “Do not covet.”
The law told Paul what is coveting and what is not coveting.
The law made Paul aware of coveting.
Because the law tells us what sin is, should we say the law of God is bad or sinful?
No, we should not say the law of God is bad or sinful.

passages.scripture: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.

lines.text: Without the law, sin is dead.
Without the law, sin has no power.
But Paul was not without law; Paul had the law of God.
And because Paul had the law, Paul sinned.
The law gave Paul a commandment.
Through the commandment sin had opportunity to produce every kind of sinful desire in Paul.
So sin seized its opportunity to produce every kind of sinful desire in Paul.

passages.scripture: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.

lines.text: Before sin, Paul once was alive.
Paul once was alive and did not yet have the law of God.
But then the commandment from the law came.
When the commandment came, sin sprang to life.
When sin sprang to life, Paul died.

passages.scripture: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.

lines.text: God gave a commandment.
The commandment promised life in exchange for obedience.
This commandment was intended to bring life.
However the same law that promises life for obedience also warns of death for sin.
And so, instead of life, the commandment brought death to Paul.
Paul discovered this.

passages.scripture: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.

lines.text: Paul heard the commandment from the law of God.
Sin used the commandment as an opportunity to deceive.
Sin deceived Paul through the commandment so that Paul would disobey the commandment.
However, the penalty from the law of God for breaking the commandment was death.
Sin used the commandment to put Paul to death.

passages.scripture: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.

lines.text: The law comes from God.
God is holy.
The law is holy.
The commandment is holy.
The commandment is righteous.
The commandment is good.

passages.scripture: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.

lines.text: The commandment is that which is good.
The commandment is from the law of God.
The commandment did not cause the death of Paul.
That which is good did not become death to Paul.
Sin was the cause of the death of Paul.
Sin used the law, which is good, to produce death in Paul.
This death showed that sin is clearly sin.
Sin became extremely sinful through the commandment.

passages.scripture: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.

lines.text: The law is spiritual.
The law comes from God and God is spirit.
Paul was not spiritual.
Paul was unspiritual.
Paul was sold as a slave to sin.

passages.scripture: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.

lines.text: Paul wanted to follow the law of God.
But Paul did not follow the law of God.
Paul hated sin.
And yet Paul sinned.
Paul did not understand the things he did.
Paul did not understand why Paul did the things he did not want to do.
Paul did not understand why Paul did not do the thing he did want to do.

passages.scripture: And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.

lines.text: Paul did not want to sin.
But Paul sinned.
Paul did what Paul did not want to do.
The law of God forbids sin.
When Paul did not want to sin, Paul was agreeing with the law.
When Paul did not want to sin, Paul was declaring that the law is good.
Paul is speaking.
Paul is a Christian.
Paul struggles with sin.
Paul wants to do good.
Paul sometimes does what he does not want to do.
If I do what I do not want to do, I agree with the law.
The law is good.

passages.scripture: In that case, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

lines.text: Because Paul didn't want to sin, it was no longer Paul who sinned.
Sin, living inside Paul, was the cause of the sin, and not Paul.

passages.scripture: I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.

lines.text: Even though Paul was a Christian, nothing good lived in the flesh of Paul.
Nothing good lived in Paul.
Paul desired to do good.
And yet, Paul could not carry out doing the good he wanted to do.
Paul could not do the good.

passages.scripture: For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.

lines.text: As a Christian, Paul wanted to do the good things that the law of God commands.
Paul wanted to obey the law.
But Paul did not obey the law.
Paul did not do the good things that he wanted to do.
And Paul did not want to disobey the law of God.
Paul did not want to do evil things.
Instead, Paul disobeyed the law of God.
Paul kept on doing the evil things that he did not want to do.

passages.scripture: And if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.

lines.text: Paul did not want to do sin.
And yet Paul sinned.
Because Paul did not want to sin, it was not Paul doing the sin.
Sin was living inside Paul.
Because Paul did not want to sin, it was sin doing the sin.
Sin living in Paul sinned, not Paul.

passages.scripture: So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.

lines.text: As a Christian, Paul wanted to do good.
However, when Paul wanted to do good, evil was present with Paul.
When Paul wanted to do good, evil was present with him.
Evil was close to Paul when he tried to do good.
Paul discovered this principle.

passages.scripture: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.

lines.text: Paul had an inner being.
In the inner being of Paul, Paul delighted in the law of God.
In the inner being of Paul, Paul wanted to obey the law of God.

passages.scripture: But I see another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.

lines.text: Paul had a body.
Besides the law of God, there was another law.
The law was at work in the body of Paul.
Paul's mind had a law.
This other law warred against the law of the mind of Paul.
This law working in Paul's body fought against the law in his mind.
The law in the mind of Paul wanted to follow God.
But the law at work in his body made him a prisoner to the law of sin.
The law of sin dwelled inside Paul.

passages.scripture: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?

lines.text: Paul was a wretched man.
Paul realized that Paul was a wretched man.
Paul struggled to not sin in his body.
The body of Paul was a body of death.
Paul felt trapped by his body of death.
Paul needed someone to rescue him from his body of death.

passages.scripture: Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.

lines.text: Jesus Christ is our Lord.
We give thanks to God.
We give thanks through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Paul served the law of God with his mind.
But Paul served the law of sin with his flesh.
